question: Should this issue accept Windows Hub as the supported Windows companion and narrow to a staged Linux-native implementation, or continue requiring first-party applications for both platforms?
rationale: Current main explicitly documents Windows Hub and leaves Linux planned, while multiple competing in-repository implementations closed over architecture, correctness, packaging, and security concerns; automation cannot choose the permanent product and ownership boundary.

options.title: Windows Hub plus staged Linux
options.body: Accept Windows Hub for Windows and define small Linux foundation milestones with explicit security, packaging, shared-contract, and proof gates.

options.title: First-party apps for both
options.body: Keep both platforms in scope and commit to repository ownership, framework choices, release infrastructure, and long-term maintenance for two native products.

options.title: External companions for both
options.body: Keep core limited to generic gateway and node contracts while vetted platform repositories own both desktop companions.

recommendation.title: Windows Hub plus staged Linux
recommendation.body: Accept Windows Hub for Windows and define small Linux foundation milestones with explicit security, packaging, shared-contract, and proof gates.

likelyOwner.reason: He opened the roadmap item, articulated the native Linux goal, and authored the current platform-status and vision wording.
